name: circular_reference_linearization
mechanism: Bacterial chromosomes and plasmids are circular molecules, but reference genomes are stored as linear FASTA sequences with an arbitrary start position. Reads that physically span the linearization point — i.e., reads that originate from the region of the genome that straddles position 1 in the FASTA — cannot align end-to-end to the reference because the reference has an artificial break at that position. These reads are either unmapped, soft-clipped, or produce split alignments. For a 4.9 Mb chromosome with 150 bp paired-end reads, approximately 300-400 read pairs (~0.03% of a 50x dataset) are affected. The result is a systematic coverage gap at position 1 and at the last ~150 bp of every contig in the reference — a telltale pattern that is invisible to aggregate mapping statistics but visible in per-position coverage analysis. Variant callers silently miss variants in these regions.

known_behaviors.tool: All short-read aligners (BWA-MEM, Bowtie2, Minimap2 sr)
known_behaviors.behavior: Coverage drops to zero or near-zero at positions 1 through ~read_length and at positions (contig_length - read_length) through contig_length. Not reported by samtools flagstat. Visible only via mosdepth or samtools depth. Silent.
Reads spanning the linearization point are split-aligned (SA supplementary tag). If the split alignment does not score well, the read is reported as soft-clipped or unmapped. Exit 0.

samples.description: Salmonella Typhimurium LT2 linearized reference — the chromosome is circular but stored as a linear FASTA starting at an arbitrary position

download.command: datasets download genome accession GCF_000006945.2 --include genome --filename genome.zip && unzip -q genome.zip && cat ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000006945.2/*.fna > assembly.fasta && rm -rf ncbi_dataset genome.zip README.md

samples.description: Salmonella Typhimurium PNUSAS576962 reads — standard Illumina paired-end, ~60x coverage

download.command: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir . SRR38945246 && mv SRR38945246_1.fastq.gz reads_1.fq.gz && mv SRR38945246_2.fastq.gz reads_2.fq.gz

ground_truth.detection: Run 'samtools depth -a' and inspect coverage at chromosome positions 1-300 and last 300 positions. Coverage should drop sharply relative to adjacent positions.

curation.notes: This challenge requires no unusual input data — it fires on any alignment of real Illumina reads to any bacterial reference genome. The LT2 reference is used here because its chromosome start position is well-documented (ori at position ~3.9 Mb, so position 1 is in the replication terminus region). The effect is small in aggregate but systematic: it creates false variant-free zones at every contig boundary in draft assemblies.
